Post-implementation and finalization evidence were mediated for real (exit_code 0, 4 passed), and implementation-report.json was promoted with status ready_for_verification -- the first such artifact ever produced by a real /work run. Verification: a real, live-dispatched Quality Engineer (agent a96d7d1edcebbc7e5) independently re-ran the narrow test command (exit_code 0, 4 passed) and returned final_verdict: pass for both acceptance criteria, promoted to verification-report.json. The orchestrator independently re-verified this pass verdict itself (not on the Quality Engineer's word alone): re-ran the same narrow command through the real test-runner Skill (ORCH-1, exit_code 0), ran the full demo-repo suite (ORCH-2, exit_code 0, 102 passed -- 101 baseline + 1 new), and confirmed via git status/git diff --stat that exactly the three claimed files changed (demo-repo/src/loanflow/explanations.py, demo-repo/src/loanflow/cli.py, demo-repo/tests/unit/test_explanations.py) with no drift and no out-of-scope or Protected Path changes. Two transport/parse failures occurred (the Architect's Research response arrived clean; the Engineer's first pre_test_requested and the Quality Engineer's first attempt_requested were both Markdown-fenced) -- each was retained verbatim as evidence, classified, and repaired via exactly one transport-only correction to the same agent id per phase, per the documented transport-repair protocol, never by locally stripping fences.
